messages:
ana: Heads-up — we need a short rolling maintenance to address a control-plane NIC image that intermittently nudges vNICs into a reset state. Not urgent but we've seen packet drops during firmware handshake under sustained load. Plan proposal: non-overlapping rolling reboots of compute racks in us-west1 and apac-west1, starting 2026-04-02 02:00 UTC (us-west1 first), 02:30 UTC (apac-west1). Each rack: 6 nodes, pause 7m per node, 2-node canary per rack, KV/prefix cache seed after each node comes back. Estimated impact: transient 5-10ms extra tail and ~2% capacity reduction per rack while node drains. Requesting oncall and capacity hedging for that window. :eyes:

mike: Sounds reasonable. Can we avoid overlapping with the large nightly batch in us-east? what's the expected spillover to regional burst pools?

ana: (typo fix) ana meant jess for capacity numbers :sweat_smile:

jess: I can provide numbers — we want to keep at least 85% live GPU capacity for latency-sensitive customers. For us-west1 rack rotation that's ~18 GPUs reserved (2 extra spare nodes). If we need spot backfill, cost delta estimated ~+$120/hr (worst-case for the window). I'll post exact capacity delta in 5m.

helen: For canary, propose this sequence: drain -> reboot -> kubelet healthcheck -> kvcache-prime -> perf smoke test (p50/p95 token latency) -> promote. Start with 2 nodes, if both pass 10m then continue. If >2 failures, abort and rollback.

ana: ops-bot runbook link?

ops-bot: Runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/vnic-reset-maintenance. Steps include drain command and backfill checklist. Use tag: maintenance:vnic-reset-20260402.

ana: quick drain command we expect to use (example):
```
kubectl drain gpu-node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=420
```
And after reboot:
```
kubectl uncordon gpu-node-42
run bench/warmup/prefix-seed.sh --region us-west1 --node gpu-node-42
```

mike: Two quick asks — will prefix cache seeding require extra io egress? and is there a risk of hitting quota limits for KV priming in apac?

jess: Prefix seeding uses cached snapshots; minimal egress. KV priming is rate-limited by controller, we've set a soft cap of 50 req/s per rack for the window. apac quota is fine but we'll keep an eye.

helen: I'll own canary smoke tests and threshold gating. Mike, can you run a short capacity plan to confirm we don't dip under 85% for any tenant?

mike: On it — will post numbers in 6m. Also make sure autoscaler cooldown is bumped to 15m to avoid premature scale-down.

sre-bot: Scheduled incident stub created: INC-20260402-VNIC. Pager rotations: oncall-engineering, infra-sre. Notifications: #incidents and #eng-infra.

jess: Capacity check: us-west1 after reserving spares -> live GPUs 88%, apac-west1 -> live GPUs 86%. Spot backfill only used if background batch starts; cost estimate stands.

ana: ok ready to proceed with the timeline. I'll post the exact node list and per-node ETA 20m before start. Please acknowledge when you read this.

mike: ack :thumbsup:

helen: ack and will be live in case canary fails.

jess: ack — I will monitor autoscaler and cost.

ops-bot: Reminder: set maintenance window tag and mute non-critical alerts for nodes under drain to avoid noise.

ana: thanks everyone. Will update with node roster and canary IDs.
